The closest match is [1], which directly studies distributional reinforcement learning in chaotic dynamical systems and explains why return distributions can evolve more regularly than individual trajectories under chaos. [1] It argues that this yields a smoother distributional Bellman objective and better conditioned learning in chaotic settings. [1]

Other nearby papers are [7] and [6], but they do not focus on chaotic dynamics: [7] proposes a distributional RL critic using diffusion bridges, and [6] develops average-reward distributional RL with a quotient-space formulation. [7, 6]
